<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000468" name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001492633_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000468_dcnt_42e2198b-795e-497e-b486-6e5ae443899d">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">9. Fair Value Measurements </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nielsen&#8217;s financial instruments include cash and cash equivalents, investments, long-term debt and derivative financial instruments. These financial instruments potentially subject Nielsen to concentrations of credit risk. To minimize the risk of credit loss, these financial instruments are primarily held with acknowledged financial institutions. The carrying value of Nielsen&#8217;s financial instruments approximate fair value, except for differences with respect to long-term, fixed and variable-rate debt. The fair value of financial instruments is generally determined by reference to market values resulting from trading on a national securities exchange or in an over-the-counter market. In cases where quoted market prices are not available, fair value is based on estimates using present value or other valuation techniques. Cash equivalents have original maturities of three months or less.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In addition, the Company has accounts receivable that are not collateralized. The Connect and Media segments service high quality clients dispersed across many geographic areas. The Company analyzes the aging of accounts receivable, historical bad debts, customer creditworthiness and current economic trends in determining the allowance for doubtful accounts.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">93</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000468_dcnt_42e2198b-795e-497e-b486-6e5ae443899d" continuedAt="F_000468_dcnt_900a3532-119d-4890-8751-8e51a484ad28">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Investments include investments in affiliates and a trading asset portfolio maintained to generate returns to offset changes in certain liabilities related to deferred compensation arrangements. Nielsen assesses declines in the value of individual investments to determine whether such decline is other than temporary and thus the investment is impaired by considering available evidence. <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000912" name="us-gaap:OtherAssetImpairmentCharges" contextRef="C_0001492633_20200101_20201231" decimals="-6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000913" name="us-gaap:OtherAssetImpairmentCharges" contextRef="C_0001492633_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000914" name="us-gaap:OtherAssetImpairmentCharges" contextRef="C_0001492633_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6">No</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> impairment charge was recorded for the years ended December 31, 2020, 2019 and 2018.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">Fair value is defined as the price that would be received from selling an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. When determining fair value, the Company considers the principal or most advantageous market in which the Company would transact, and also considers assumptions that market participants would use when pricing the asset or liability, such as inherent risk, transfer restrictions, and risk of non-performance</span><span style="color:#000000;">. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There are three levels of inputs that may be used to measure fair value: </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Financial Assets and Liabilities Measured on a Recurring Basis </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">The Company&#8217;s financial assets and liabilities are measured and recorded at fair value, except for equity method investments and long-term debt. Financial assets and liabilities are classified in their entirety based on the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurements. The Company&#8217;s assessment of the significance of a particular input to the fair value measurements requires judgment, and may affect the valuation of the assets and liabilities being measured and their placement within the fair value hierarchy. In addition, the Company records changes in the fair value of equity investments with readily determinable fair values in net income rather than in accumulated other comprehensive income/(loss). Investments that do not have readily determinable fair values are recognized at cost minus impairment, if any, plus or minus changes resulting from observable price changes in orderly transactions for the identical or a similar investment of the same issuer. The adjustments related to the observable price changes will also be recognized in net income</span><span style="color:#000000;">. </span></p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000512" name="us-gaap:FairValueByBalanceSheetGroupingTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001492633_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000512_dcnt_21dbdb3f-91d6-4137-a24b-af87100c17d3">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Derivative Financial Instruments </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nielsen primarily uses interest rate swap derivative instruments to manage the risk that changes in interest rates will affect the cash flows of its underlying debt obligations. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">To qualify for hedge accounting, the hedging relationship must meet several conditions with respect to documentation, probability of occurrence, hedge effectiveness and reliability of measurement. Nielsen documents the relationship between hedging instruments and hedged items, as well as its risk management objective and strategy for undertaking various hedge transactions as well as the hedge effectiveness assessment, both at the hedge inception and on an ongoing basis. Nielsen recognizes all derivatives at fair value either as assets or liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets and changes in the fair values of such instruments are recognized currently in earnings unless specific hedge accounting criteria are met. If specific cash flow hedge accounting criteria are met, Nielsen recognizes the changes in fair value of these instruments in accumulated other comprehensive income/(loss). </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nielsen manages exposure to possible defaults on derivative financial instruments by monitoring the concentration of risk that Nielsen has with any individual bank and through the use of minimum credit quality standards for all counterparties. Nielsen does not require collateral or other security in relation to derivative financial instruments. A derivative contract entered into between Nielsen or certain of its subsidiaries and a counterparty that was also a lender under Nielsen&#8217;s senior secured credit facilities at the time the derivative contract was entered into is guaranteed under the senior secured credit facilities by Nielsen and certain of its subsidiaries (see Note 12 &#8211; (&#8220;Long-term Debt and Other Financing Arrangements&#8221;) for more information). Since it is Nielsen&#8217;s policy to only enter into derivative contracts with banks of internationally acknowledged standing, Nielsen considers the counterparty risk to be remote. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">It is Nielsen&#8217;s policy to have an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (&#8220;ISDA&#8221;) Master Agreement established with every bank with which it has entered into any derivative contract. Under each of these ISDA Master Agreements, Nielsen agrees to settle only the net amount of the combined market values of all derivative contracts outstanding with any one counterparty should that counterparty default. Certain of the ISDA Master Agreements contain cross-default provisions where if the Company either defaults in payment obligations under its credit facility or if such obligations are accelerated by the lenders, then the Company could also be declared in default on its derivative obligations. At December 31, 2020, Nielsen had no material exposure to potential economic losses due to counterparty credit default risk or cross-default risk on its derivative financial instruments. </p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">95</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000468_dcnt_4c3af5ae-0806-4d7c-a742-dd59acfd0983" continuedAt="F_000468_dcnt_fe5a1cf9-5374-44cc-8f98-07f5535d18ce">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Interest Rate Risk </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nielsen is exposed to cash flow interest rate risk on the floating-rate U.S.&#160;Dollar and Euro Term Loans, and uses floating-to-fixed interest rate swaps to hedge this exposure. For these derivatives, Nielsen reports the after-tax gain or loss from the effective portion of the hedge as a component of accumulated other comprehensive income/(loss)&#160;and reclassifies it into earnings in the same period or periods in which the hedged transaction affects earnings, and within the same income statement line item as the impact of the hedged transaction.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In May 2019, the Company entered into a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000941" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapDerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis_nlsnnvUsDollarTermLoanFloatingToFixedRateSwapsMaturingOnJulyTwentyThreeMember_20190531" decimals="INF" scale="6">150</ix:nonFraction> million aggregate notional amount <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000942">four-year</span> forward interest rate swap agreement with a starting date of July 9, 2019. This derivative has been designated as an interest rate cash flow hedge.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In March 2019, the Company entered into a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000944" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapDerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis_nlsnnvUsDollarTermLoanFloatingToFixedRateSwapsMaturingOnAprilTwentyThreeMember_20190331" decimals="INF" scale="6">150</ix:nonFraction> million aggregate notional amount <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000945">four-year</span> forward interest rate swap agreement with a starting date of April 9, 2019. <p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000468_dcnt_60078036-3d85-4191-b9c9-09260ff1abe5">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Assets and Liabilities Measured at Fair Value on a Nonrecurring Basis </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company is required, on a nonrecurring basis, to adjust the carrying value for certain assets using fair value measurements. The Company&#8217;s equity method investments, and non-financial assets, such as goodwill, intangible assets, and property, plant and equipment, are measured at fair value when there is an indicator of impairment and recorded at fair value only when an impairment charge is recognized. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">During 2020, Nielsen decided to exit smaller, underperforming markets, non-core businesses and a product line and concluded that this decision represented an impairment indicator for the long-lived assets within those markets and businesses.&#160;&#160;In addition, during the fourth quarter of 2020, Nielsen identified a change in the extent to which certain self-developed software would be utilized and concluded this represented an impairment indicator.&#160;&#160;To the extent that the carrying value of the assets exceeded the sum of the future undiscounted cash flows, we measured an impairment charge using a discounted cash flow method for estimation of the assets&#8217; fair value.&#160;&#160;During the year ended December 31, 2020, we recognized a pre-tax non-cash impairment charge associated with amortizable intangible assets of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000994" name="us-gaap:AssetImpairmentCharges" contextRef="C_0001492633_20200101_20201231" decimals="-6" scale="6">88</ix:nonFraction> million and property, plant and equipment of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000995" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfLongLivedAssetsHeldForUse" contextRef="C_0001492633_20200101_20201231" decimals="-6" scale="6">8</ix:nonFraction> million.&#160;&#160;</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Other indefinite-lived intangible assets are each tested for impairment on an annual basis and whenever events or circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of such asset may not be recoverable. The impairment test for other indefinite-lived intangible assets consists of a comparison of the fair value of the intangible asset with its carrying amount. If the carrying amount of the intangible asset exceeds its fair value, an impairment loss is recognized in an amount equal to that excess. The estimates of fair value of trade names and trademarks are determined using a &#8220;relief from royalty&#8221; discounted cash flow valuation methodology. Significant assumptions inherent in this methodology include estimates of royalty rates and discount rates.&#160;&#160;Discount rate assumptions are based on an assessment of the risk inherent in the respective intangible assets.&#160;&#160;The discount rates we used in our 2020 evaluation were between <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000996" name="nlsnnv:DiscountRate" contextRef="C_0001492633_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapMeasurementInputTypeAxis_us-gaapMeasurementInputDiscountRateMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="3" scale="-2">12.1</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000997" name="nlsnnv:DiscountRate" contextRef="C_0001492633_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapMeasurementInputTypeAxis_us-gaapMeasurementInputDiscountRateMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="4" scale="-2">13.35</ix:nonFraction>%. Assumptions about royalty rates are based on the rates at which comparable trade names and trademarks are being licensed in the marketplace. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">During the year ended December 31, 2020, we recognized a pre-tax non-cash impairment charge associated with the indefinite -lived intangible asset within our Connect segment of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000998" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsIndefinitelivedExcludingGoodwill" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapStatementBusinessSegmentsAxis_nlsnnvConnectMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="-6" scale="6">88</ix:nonFraction> million. The nonrecurring fair value amount (as measured at the time of the adjustment) for the indefinite-lived tradename remeasured to fair value on a nonrecurring basis during the fiscal year and still held at December 31, 2020 was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000999" name="us-gaap:IndefiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsExcludingGoodwill" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapFairValueByMeasurementFrequencyAxis_us-gaapFairValueMeasurementsNonrecurringMember_us-gaapIndefiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis_us-gaapTradeNamesMember_20201231" decimals="-6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="6">1,130</ix:nonFraction> million.&#160;&#160; </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company did not measure any other material non-financial assets or liabilities at fair value during the year ended December 31, 2019.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000469" name="us-gaap:RestructuringAndRelatedActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001492633_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000469_dcnt_1069094a-5810-4d99-bce4-e69bc11049d7">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">10. Restructuring Activities </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Optimization Initiatives</p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#212529;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In June, 2020, Nielsen announced a broad-based optimization plan to drive permanent cost savings and operational efficiencies, as well as to position the Company for greater profitability and growth. The plan was substantially completed in 2020. </p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#212529;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">Nielsen incurred $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001000" name="us-gaap:RestructuringCharges" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapRestructuringPlanAxis_nlsnnvBroadBasedOptimizationPlanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="-6" scale="6">144</ix:nonFraction> million of restructuring charges in the year ended December 31, 2020. These charges mostly represent severance costs related to employee separation packages. </span><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;color:#000000;">The amounts are calculated based on salary levels and past service periods.</span><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;"> </span><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;color:#000000;">Severance costs are generally charged to earnings when planned employee terminations are approved</span>.</p></ix:nonNumeric>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Of the $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001017" name="us-gaap:RestructuringReserve" contextRef="C_0001492633_20201231" decimals="-6" scale="6">64</ix:nonFraction> million in remaining liabilities for restructuring actions, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001018" name="us-gaap:RestructuringReserveCurrent" contextRef="C_0001492633_20201231" decimals="-6" scale="6">58</ix:nonFraction> million is expected to be paid within one year and is classified as a current liability within the consolidated financial statements as of December 31, 2020. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:4pt;">&#160;</p></ix:continuation>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:4pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:8pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000470" name="us-gaap:PensionAndOtherPostretirementBenefitsDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001492633_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000470_dcnt_14b4004b-f3b2-4b9b-878c-f554a1e253c6">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">11. Pensions and Other Post-Retirement Benefits </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nielsen sponsors both funded and unfunded defined benefit pension plans (the &#8220;Pension Plans&#8221;) and post-retirement medical plans for some if its employees in the U.S. and other international locations. Pension costs, in respect of defined benefit pension plans, primarily represent the increase in the actuarial present value of the obligation for pension benefits based on employee service during the year and the interest on this obligation in respect of employee service in previous years, net of the expected return on plan assets. Differences between this expected return and the actual return on these plan assets and actuarial changes are not recognized in the statement of operations, unless the accumulated differences and changes exceed a certain threshold. Nielsen recognizes obligations for contributions to defined contribution pension plans as expenses in the statement of operations as they are incurred.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The determination of benefit obligations and expenses is based on actuarial models. In order to measure benefit costs and obligations using these models, critical assumptions are made with regard to the discount rate, the expected return on plan assets and the assumed rate of compensation increases. Nielsen provides retiree medical benefits to a limited number of participants in the U.S. Therefore, retiree medical care cost trend rates are not a significant driver of our post retirement costs. Management reviews these critical assumptions at least annually. Other assumptions involve demographic factors such as turnover, retirement and mortality rates. Management reviews these assumptions periodically and updates them as necessary.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The discount rate is the rate at which the benefit obligations could be effectively settled. For Nielsen&#8217;s U.S. plans, the discount rate is based on a bond portfolio that includes only long-term bonds with an Aa rating, or equivalent, from a major rating agency. For the non-U.S. plans, the discount rate is set by reference to market yields on high-quality corporate bonds. Nielsen believes the timing and amount of cash flows related to the bonds in these portfolios are expected to match the estimated payment benefit streams of our plans.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company uses the spot rate approach to calculate the discount rate for its retirement benefit plans.&#160;&#160;Under the spot-rate approach, the Company uses individual spot rates along the yield curve that correspond with the timing of each future cash outflow for benefit payments in order to calculate interest cost and service cost within net periodic benefit costs.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">To determine the expected long-term rate of return on pension plan assets, Nielsen considers, for each country, the structure of the asset portfolio and the expected rates of return for each of the components. For Nielsen&#8217;s U.S. plans, a <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001019" name="nlsnnv:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingNetPeriodicBenefitCostRateOfCompensationDecrease" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapRetirementPlanSponsorLocationAxis_countryUS_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="-4">50</ix:nonFraction> basis point decrease in </p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">99</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nielsen&#8217;s primary objective with regard to the investment of the Pension Plans&#8217; assets is to ensure that in each individual plan, sufficient funds are available to satisfy future benefit obligations. The valuation methodology is applied consistently from period to period. </p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Covenants </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Amendment Agreement and the Credit Agreement, as amended by Amendment No. 1 (together the &#8220;Secured Credit Agreements&#8221;) contain a number of covenants that, among other things, restrict, subject to certain exceptions, the ability of Nielsen Holding and Finance B.V. and its restricted subsidiaries (which together constitute most of Nielsen&#8217;s subsidiaries) to incur additional indebtedness or guarantees, incur liens and engage in sale and leaseback transactions, make certain loans and investments, declare dividends, make payments or redeem or repurchase capital stock, engage in certain mergers, acquisitions and other business combinations, prepay, redeem or purchase certain indebtedness, amend or otherwise alter terms of certain indebtedness, sell certain assets, transact with affiliates, enter into agreements limiting subsidiary distributions and alter the business they conduct. These entities are restricted, subject to certain exceptions, in their ability to transfer their net assets to Nielsen. Such restricted net assets amounted to approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001689" name="us-gaap:AmountOfRestrictedNetAssetsForConsolidatedAndUnconsolidatedSubsidiaries" contextRef="C_0001492633_20201231" decimals="-8" scale="9">1.9</ix:nonFraction> billion at December 31, 2020. The Amendment Agreement contains a total leverage covenant that requires the Covenant Parties (as defined in the Amendment Agreement) maintain a ratio of Consolidated Total Net Debt (as defined in the Amendment Agreement) to Consolidated EBITDA (as defined in the Amendment Agreement) at or below <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001690" name="nlsnnv:LeverageRatio" contextRef="C_0001492633_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">5.50</ix:nonFraction> to 1.00, measured at the end of each calendar quarter for the four quarters most recently ended. Neither Nielsen nor TNC B.V. is currently bound by any financial or negative covenants contained in the Secured Credit Agreements. The Secured Credit Agreements also contain certain customary affirmative covenants and events of default. Certain significant financial covenants are described further below.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Failure to comply with the financial covenant described above would result in an event of default under Nielsen&#8217;s Amendment Agreement unless waived by certain of Nielsen&#8217;s term lenders and Nielsen&#8217;s revolving lenders. An event of default under Nielsen&#8217;s Amendment Agreement can result in the acceleration of Nielsen&#8217;s indebtedness under the facilities thereunder, which in turn would result in an event of default and possible acceleration of indebtedness under the Credit Agreement, as amended by Amendment No. 1, </p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">109</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000471_dcnt_c788cfd4-9957-497e-babb-69ce7ba7f63d">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">and the agreements governing Nielsen&#8217;s debt securities as well. As Nielsen&#8217;s failure to comply with the financial covenant described above can cause Nielsen to go into default under the agreements governing Nielsen&#8217;s indebtedness, management believes that Nielsen&#8217;s Amendment Agreement and this covenant are material to Nielsen. As of December 31, 2020, Nielsen was in full compliance with the financial covenant described above. </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Pursuant to the terms of Nielsen&#8217;s Secured Credit Agreements, Nielsen is subject to making mandatory prepayments on the term loans outstanding thereunder to the extent in any full calendar year Nielsen generates Excess Cash Flow (&#8220;ECF&#8221;), as defined in the Secured Credit Agreements. The percentage of ECF that must be applied as a repayment under either Secured Credit Agreement is a function of several factors, including Nielsen&#8217;s ratio of total net debt to Covenant EBITDA, as well other adjustments, including any voluntary term loan repayments and permanent reductions of revolving credit commitments made in the course of the calendar year. To the extent any mandatory repayment is required pursuant to this ECF clause&#59; such payment must generally occur on or around the time of the delivery of the annual consolidated financial statements to the applicable lenders. At December 31, 2020, Nielsen&#8217;s ratio of total net debt to Covenant EBITDA was less than <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001691" name="nlsnnv:DebtInstrumentCovenantCalculatedNetDebtToConsolidatedEBITDARatio" contextRef="C_0001492633_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">5.00</ix:nonFraction> to 1.00 and therefore no mandatory repayment was required. Nielsen&#8217;s next ECF measurement date will occur upon completion of the 2021 results, and although Nielsen do not expect to be required to issue any mandatory repayments in 2021 or beyond, it is uncertain at this time if any such payments will be required in future periods. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Revolving Credit Facility </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Amendment Agreement contains a senior secured revolving credit facility with aggregate revolving credit commitments of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001692" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_nlsnnvNewRevolvingLineOfCreditMember_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="6">850</ix:nonFraction> million and a final maturity of <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001693" name="nlsnnv:LineOfCreditFacilityExpirationDate" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_nlsnnvNewRevolvingLineOfCreditMember_20160101_20161231" format="ixt:datemonthyearen">July 2023</ix:nonNumeric> under which Nielsen Finance LLC, TNC (US) Holdings, Inc., and Nielsen Holding and Finance B.V. can borrow revolving loans. The revolving credit facility can also be used for letters of credit, guarantees and swingline loans.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The senior secured revolving credit facility is provided under the Amendment Agreement and so contains covenants and restrictions as noted above with respect to the Amendment Agreement. Obligations under the revolving credit facility are guaranteed by the same entities that guarantee obligations under the Amendment Agreement. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:8pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December 31, 2020, Nielsen had <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001694" name="nlsnnv:OutstandingBorrowings" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20201231" decimals="-6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6">zero</ix:nonFraction> borrowings outstanding and outstanding letters of credit of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001696" name="us-gaap:LettersOfCreditOutstandingAmount" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20201231" decimals="-6" scale="6">18</ix:nonFraction> million.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2019, Nielsen had <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001695" name="nlsnnv:OutstandingBorrowings" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20191231" decimals="-6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6">zero</ix:nonFraction> borrowings outstanding and outstanding letters of credit of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001697" name="us-gaap:LettersOfCreditOutstandingAmount" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">17</ix:nonFraction> million. As of December 31, 2020, Nielsen had $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001698" name="nlsnnv:CreditFacilityAvailableBorrowingLine" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20201231" decimals="-6" scale="6">832</ix:nonFraction> million available for borrowing under the revolving credit facility.<span style="font-style:italic;"> </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:8pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Other Transactions</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Effective July&#160;1, 2010, the Company designated its Euro denominated variable rate senior secured term loans as non-derivative hedges of its net investment in a European subsidiary. Gains or losses attributable to fluctuations in the Euro as compared to the U.S.&#160;Dollar associated with this debenture were recorded to the cumulative translation adjustment within shareholders&#8217; equity, net of income tax. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Debt-Issuance Costs </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The costs related to the issuance of debt are presented as a deduction from the corresponding debt liability and amortized to interest expense using the effective interest method over the life of the related debt.&#160;&#160;<span style="font-style:italic;"> </span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Finance Lease and Other Obligations</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nielsen finances certain computer equipment, software, buildings and automobiles under finance leases and related transactions. These arrangements do not include terms of renewal, purchase options, or escalation clauses.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:2pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Assets under finance lease are recorded within property, plant and equipment. See Note 8 &#8220;Property, Plant and Equipment.&#8221; Liabilities under finance leases are recorded within long-term debt and other financing obligations above. See Note 5 &#8220;Leases&#8221; for more information on finance leases and other financing obligations referenced in this note.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000473" name="us-gaap:DisclosureOfCompensationRelatedCostsShareBasedPaymentsTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001492633_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000473_dcnt_0d44bb23-0d4b-46e9-9f34-98b318f37d96">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">14. Share-based Compensation </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nielsen measures the cost of all share-based payments, including stock options, at fair value on the grant date and recognizes such costs within the consolidated statements of operations. Nielsen recognizes the expense of its options that cliff vest using the straight-line method. For those that vest over time, an accelerated graded vesting is used. The Company recorded $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001760" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" contextRef="C_0001492633_20200101_20201231" decimals="-6" scale="6">53</ix:nonFraction> million, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001761" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" contextRef="C_0001492633_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">50</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001762" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" contextRef="C_0001492633_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">35</ix:nonFraction> million of expense associated with share-based compensation for the years ended December 31, 2020, 2019 and 2018, respectively. The tax benefit related to the share-based compensation expense was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001763" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationTaxBenefitFromCompensationExpense" contextRef="C_0001492633_20200101_20201231" decimals="-6" scale="6">5</ix:nonFraction> million, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001764" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationTaxBenefitFromCompensationExpense" contextRef="C_0001492633_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">6</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001765" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationTaxBenefitFromCompensationExpense" contextRef="C_0001492633_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">5</ix:nonFraction> million for each of the respective periods.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nielsen has an equity-based, management compensation plan (&#8220;Equity Participation Plan&#8221; or &#8220;EPP&#8221;) to align compensation for certain key executives with the performance of the Company. Under this plan, certain of the Company&#8217;s executives may be granted stock options, stock appreciation rights, restricted stock, restricted stock units and dividend equivalent rights in the shares of the Company or purchase its shares. In connection with the completion of Nielsen&#8217;s initial public offering of common stock on January 31, 2011 (and further amended), the Company implemented the Nielsen 2010 Stock Incentive Plan (the &#8220;Prior Plan&#8221;) and suspended further grants under the EPP. In 2019, the Company replaced the Nielsen 2010 Stock Incentive Plan with the Nielsen 2019 Stock Incentive Plan (the &#8220;Stock Incentive Plan&#8221;). The Stock Incentive Plan is the source of new equity-based awards permitting the Company to grant to its key employees, directors and other service providers the following types of awards: incentive stock options, non-qualified stock options, stock appreciation rights, restricted stock, restricted stock units and other awards valued in whole or in part by reference to shares of Nielsen&#8217;s common stock and performance-based awards denominated in shares or cash.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Under the Stock Incentive Plan, Nielsen granted <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001768" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsGrantsInPeriodGross" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_nlsnnvTimeBasedStockOptionsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvStockIncentivePlanMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">750,000</ix:nonFraction> time-based stock options to purchase shares during the year ended December 31, 2018.&#160;&#160;<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001766" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsGrantsInPeriodGross" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_nlsnnvTimeBasedStockOptionsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvStockIncentivePlanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001767" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsGrantsInPeriodGross" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_nlsnnvTimeBasedStockOptionsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvStockIncentivePlanMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">No</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> time-based stock options to purchase shares were granted during the years ended December 31, 2020 and 2019. As of December 31, 2020, the total number of shares authorized for award of options or other equity-based awards was <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001769" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" contextRef="C_0001492633_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">10,420,826</ix:nonFraction> under the Stock Incentive Plan. This includes the <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001770" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvStockIncentivePlanMember_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">7,200,000</ix:nonFraction> newly authorized shares under the Stock Incentive Plan and the <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001771" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvTwoThousandAndTenStockIncentivePlanMember_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">3,220,826</ix:nonFraction> shares reserved for issuance from the Prior Plan. The 2018 time-based awards become exercisable over a <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001772" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingPeriod1" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_nlsnnvTimeBasedStockOptionsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvStockIncentivePlanMember_20180101_20181231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">three year</ix:nonNumeric> vesting period at a rate of <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001773" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRights" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_nlsnnvTimeBasedStockOptionsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvStockIncentivePlanMember_20180101_20181231"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001774" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRightsPercentage" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_nlsnnvTimeBasedStockOptionsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvStockIncentivePlanMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="3" scale="-2">33.3</ix:nonFraction>% per year</ix:nonNumeric> on the anniversary date of the award, and are tied to the executives&#8217; continuing employment.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair values of the time-based awards granted during 2018 were estimated using the Black-Scholes option pricing model with the expected volatility based on the Company&#8217;s historical volatility.&#160;&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000532" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfShareBasedPaymentAwardStockOptionsValuationAssumptionsTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001492633_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The following assumptions were used for the grants of time-based awards during 2018: &#160;</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the years ended December 31, 2020 and 2019, there were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001814" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsGrantsInPeriodGross" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_nlsnnvTimeBasedStockOptionsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvStockIncentivePlanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001815" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsGrantsInPeriodGross" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_nlsnnvTimeBasedStockOptionsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvStockIncentivePlanMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> time-based only options granted and the aggregate fair value of options vested was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001816" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardOptionsVestedInPeriodFairValue1" contextRef="C_0001492633_20200101_20201231" decimals="-6" scale="6">3</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001817" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardOptionsVestedInPeriodFairValue1" contextRef="C_0001492633_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">5</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively. As of December 31, 2018, the weighted-average grant date fair value of the options granted was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_001818" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsGrantsInPeriodWeightedAverageGrantDateFairValue" contextRef="C_0001492633_20180101_20181231" decimals="2">2.16</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and the aggregate fair value of options vested was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001819" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardOptionsVestedInPeriodFairValue1" contextRef="C_0001492633_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">6</ix:nonFraction> million.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At December 31, 2020, there was an insignificant amount of unearned share-based compensation related to stock options (net of estimated forfeitures) which the Company expects to record as share-based compensation expense over the next year. The compensation expense related to the time-based awards is amortized over the term of the award using the graded vesting method. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The intrinsic value of the options exercised during the year ended December 31, 2020 was <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001820" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsExercisesInPeriodTotalIntrinsicValue" contextRef="C_0001492633_20200101_20201231" decimals="-6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6">zero</ix:nonFraction> as there were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001822" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesStockOptionsExercised" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_nlsnnvTimeBasedStockOptionsMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction> time-based options exercised. The intrinsic value of the options exercised during the year ended December 31, 2019 was insignificant. The intrinsic value of the options exercised during the year ended December 31, 2018 was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001821" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsExercisesInPeriodTotalIntrinsicValue" contextRef="C_0001492633_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">6</ix:nonFraction> million.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Under the Nielsen Stock Incentive Plan, Nielsen granted <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001823" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsGrantsInPeriodGross" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_nlsnnvTimeAndPerformanceBasedStockOptionsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvStockIncentivePlanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">200,000</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001825" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsGrantsInPeriodGross" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_nlsnnvTimeAndPerformanceBasedStockOptionsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvStockIncentivePlanMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">2,524,176</ix:nonFraction> time and performance based stock options to purchase shares during the years ended December 31, 2020 and 2018, respectively.&#160;&#160;There were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001824" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsGrantsInPeriodGross" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_nlsnnvTimeAndPerformanceBasedStockOptionsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvStockIncentivePlanMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction> time and performance based stock options granted during the year ended December 31, 2019. The weighted average grant date fair value of the awards in 2020 and 2018 were $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_001826" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriodWeightedAverageGrantDateFairValue" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_nlsnnvTimeAndPerformanceBasedStockOptionsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvStockIncentivePlanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="2">3.56</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_001827" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriodWeightedAverageGrantDateFairValue" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_nlsnnvTimeAndPerformanceBasedStockOptionsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvStockIncentivePlanMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="2">3.09</ix:nonFraction>. The performance aspect of the award is achieved based on the performance of Nielsen&#8217;s stock price. If the performance obligations are satisfied, the award will become exercisable over a <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001828" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingPeriod1" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_nlsnnvTimeAndPerformanceBasedStockOptionsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvStockIncentivePlanMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">three year</ix:nonNumeric> vesting period at a rate of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001829" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRightsPercentage" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_nlsnnvTimeAndPerformanceBasedStockOptionsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvStockIncentivePlanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="3" scale="-2">33.3</ix:nonFraction>% per year on the anniversary date of the award, and are tied to the executives&#8217; continuing employment. As of December 31, 2020, there was approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001830" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognizedStockOptions" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_nlsnnvTimeAndPerformanceBasedStockOptionsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvStockIncentivePlanMember_20201231" decimals="-6" scale="6">1</ix:nonFraction> million of unearned share-based compensation related to performance stock options (net of estimated forfeitures) which the Company expects to record as share-based compensation over the next <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001831" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognizedPeriodForRecognition1" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_nlsnnvTimeAndPerformanceBasedStockOptionsMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvStockIncentivePlanMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">three years</ix:nonNumeric>. </p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </p>
<p style="margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In 2016, the Company implemented the Nielsen Holdings plc 2016 Employee Share Purchase Plan (the ESPP) and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001924" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvTwoThousandSixteenEmployeeSharePurchasePlanMember_20161231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">2,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares were authorized for issuance under the ESPP. There were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001925" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesEmployeeStockPurchasePlans" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvTwoThousandSixteenEmployeeSharePurchasePlanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">266,984</ix:nonFraction>, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001926" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesEmployeeStockPurchasePlans" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvTwoThousandSixteenEmployeeSharePurchasePlanMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">201,637</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001927" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesEmployeeStockPurchasePlans" contextRef="C_0001492633_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_nlsnnvTwoThousandSixteenEmployeeSharePurchasePlanMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">174,246</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares issued under the ESPP in 2020, 2019 and 2018, respectively.&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></ix:continuation>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000474" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001492633_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000474_dcnt_f165f2a1-c054-42b9-9d68-490b29499b6e">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">15. Income Taxes </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.84%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nielsen provides for income taxes utilizing the asset and liability method of accounting for income taxes. Under this method, deferred income taxes are recorded to reflect the tax consequences in future years of differences between the tax basis of assets and liabilities and their financial reporting amounts at each balance sheet date, based on enacted tax laws and statutory tax rates applicable to the periods in which the differences are expected to affect taxable income. If it is determined that it is more likely than not that future tax benefits associated with a deferred tax asset will not be realized, a valuation allowance is provided. The effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a change in the tax rates is recognized in the consolidated statements of operations as an adjustment to income tax expense in the period that includes the enactment date.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.84%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company records a liability for unrecognized tax benefits resulting from uncertain tax positions taken or expected to be taken in a tax return. Such tax positions are, based solely on their technical merits, more likely than not to be sustained upon examination by taxing authorities and reflect the largest amount of benefit, determined on a cumulative probability basis that is more likely than not to be realized upon settlement with the applicable taxing authority with full knowledge of all relevant information. The Company recognizes interest and penalties, if any, related to unrecognized tax benefits in income tax expense.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.84%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On December 22, 2017, the TCJA was signed into law and significantly changed the way the U.S. taxes corporations. The TCJA reduced the U.S. federal corporate income tax rate from <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001928" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" contextRef="C_0001492633_20170101_20171231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">35</ix:nonFraction> percent to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001929" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" contextRef="C_0001492633_20180101_20181231" decimals="INF" scale="-2"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001930" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" contextRef="C_0001492633_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="-2"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001931" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" contextRef="C_0001492633_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">21</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> percent and created a territorial-style taxing system. The TCJA required companies to pay a one-time transition tax on earnings of certain foreign subsidiaries that were previously deferred and also created new taxes on certain types of foreign earnings. As of December 31, 2017, we made a reasonable estimate of the (a) effects on our existing deferred tax balances, and (b) the one-time transition tax. Consequently, our fourth quarter of 2017 and full year 2017 results of operations reflected a non-cash provisional net expense of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001932" name="nlsnnv:TaxCutsAndJobsActOf2017IncompleteAccountingNonCashProvisionalNetExpenseBenefit" contextRef="C_0001492633_20171001_20171231" decimals="-6" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001933" name="nlsnnv:TaxCutsAndJobsActOf2017IncompleteAccountingNonCashProvisionalNetExpenseBenefit" contextRef="C_0001492633_20170101_20171231" decimals="-6" scale="6">104</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> million. We finalized our accounting for the TCJA in December of 2018 and our results for the fourth quarter of 2018 and full year 2018 results of operations reflect, in accordance with SAB 118, a reduction in tax expense of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001934" name="us-gaap:TaxCutsAndJobsActOf2017ChangeInTaxRateDeferredTaxLiabilityIncomeTaxBenefit" contextRef="C_0001492633_20181001_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001935" name="us-gaap:TaxCutsAndJobsActOf2017ChangeInTaxRateDeferredTaxLiabilityIncomeTaxBenefit" contextRef="C_0001492633_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">252</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> million as an adjustment to the 2017 provisional expense. This was primarily comprised of a net tax benefit of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001936" name="nlsnnv:TaxCutsAndJobsActOf2017IncompleteAccountingChangeInTaxRateDeferredTaxLiabilityProvisionalIncomeTaxBenefitRelatedToTransitionTaxIncludingWithholdingTaxes" contextRef="C_0001492633_20181001_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001937" name="nlsnnv:TaxCutsAndJobsActOf2017IncompleteAccountingChangeInTaxRateDeferredTaxLiabilityProvisionalIncomeTaxBenefitRelatedToTransitionTaxIncludingWithholdingTaxes" contextRef="C_0001492633_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">57</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> million relating to finalizing the calculation of the transition tax (including withholding taxes) together with a net tax benefit of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001938" name="nlsnnv:TaxCutsAndJobsActOf2017IncompleteAccountingChangeInTaxRateDeferredTaxLiabilityProvisionalIncomeTaxBenefitAssociatedToReMeasurementOfDeferredTaxes" contextRef="C_0001492633_20181001_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001939" name="nlsnnv:TaxCutsAndJobsActOf2017IncompleteAccountingChangeInTaxRateDeferredTaxLiabilityProvisionalIncomeTaxBenefitAssociatedToReMeasurementOfDeferredTaxes" contextRef="C_0001492633_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">195</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> million associated with the re-measurement of our deferred taxes.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.84%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The TCJA imposed a U.S. tax on global intangible low taxed income (&#8220;GILTI&#8221;) that is earned by certain foreign affiliates owned by a U.S. shareholder and was intended to tax earnings of a foreign corporation that are deemed to be in excess of certain threshold return. As of December 31, 2018, Nielsen made a policy decision and elected to treat taxes on GILTI as a current period expense and have reflected as such in the financial statements for the years ended December 31, 2019 and December 31, 2020.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">115</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000474_dcnt_f165f2a1-c054-42b9-9d68-490b29499b6e" continuedAt="F_000474_dcnt_90632191-fbe7-4a84-b962-fa5259307063">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As part of an intercompany restructuring during the year ended December 31, 2018, we transferred certain intellectual property assets between wholly-owned legal entities in non-U.S. tax jurisdictions. As the impact of the transfer was the result of an intra-entity transaction, the resulting gain on the transfer was eliminated for purposes of the consolidated financial statements.&#160;&#160;The transferring entity recognized a gain on the transfer of assets that was not subject to income tax in its local jurisdiction.&#160;In accordance with ASU 2016-16, which the Company adopted in the first quarter of 2018, Nielsen recorded an income tax benefit of approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001940" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" contextRef="C_0001492633_20180101_20180331" decimals="-6" sign="-" scale="6">193</ix:nonFraction> million</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Throughout 2019 and 2020, ongoing federal and international audits were effectively settled in certain tax jurisdictions and the impact was recorded accordingly the financial statements.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.84%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Realization of deferred tax assets is based, in part, on Nielsen&#8217;s judgment and various factors including reversal of deferred tax liabilities, Nielsen&#8217;s ability to generate future taxable income in jurisdictions where such assets have arisen and potential tax planning strategies. Valuation allowances are recorded in order to reduce the deferred tax assets to the amount expected to be realized in the future.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.84%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At December 31, 2020 and 2019 the Company had net operating loss carryforwards of approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002069" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001492633_20201231" decimals="-6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="6">1,939</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002068" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001492633_20191231" decimals="-6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="6">2,066</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively, which begin to expire in <ix:nonNumeric id="F_002072" name="nlsnnv:OperatingLossCarryforwardExpirationDates" contextRef="C_0001492633_20200101_20201231">2021</ix:nonNumeric>. In addition, the Company had tax credit carryforwards of approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002071" name="nlsnnv:DeferredTaxAssetsGrossTaxCreditCarryForwards" contextRef="C_0001492633_20201231" decimals="-6" scale="6">192</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002070" name="nlsnnv:DeferredTaxAssetsGrossTaxCreditCarryForwards" contextRef="C_0001492633_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">186</ix:nonFraction> million at December 31, 2020 and 2019, respectively, which begin to expire in <ix:nonNumeric id="F_002073" name="nlsnnv:DeferredTaxAssetsOperatingLossCarryforwardsExpirationYear" contextRef="C_0001492633_20200101_20201231">2021</ix:nonNumeric>.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.84%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In certain jurisdictions, the Company has operating losses and other tax attributes that, due to the uncertainty of achieving sufficient profits to utilize these operating loss carryforwards and tax credit carryforwards, the Company currently believes it is more likely than not that a portion of these losses will not be realized. Therefore, the Company had a valuation allowance of approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002075" name="nlsnnv:ValuationAllowanceOnTaxCreditLossCarryforwardsAndDeferredTaxAssetsRelatedToOtherTemporaryDifferences" contextRef="C_0001492633_20201231" decimals="-6" scale="6">647</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002074" name="nlsnnv:ValuationAllowanceOnTaxCreditLossCarryforwardsAndDeferredTaxAssetsRelatedToOtherTemporaryDifferences" contextRef="C_0001492633_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">636</ix:nonFraction> million at December 31, 2020 and 2019, respectively, related to net operating loss carryforwards, tax credit carryforwards and deferred tax assets related to other temporary differences.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.84%;color:#222222;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">With respect to the outside basis differences of &#8220;domestic&#8221; subsidiaries, in each taxing jurisdiction where a tiered ownership structure exists, the Company has confirmed that one or more viable tax planning strategies exists in each separate taxing jurisdiction that it could, and would - if required - employ to eliminate any income tax liability on such outside basis differences. In addition, resulting from TCJA, the company no longer asserts that all foreign undistributed earnings will be permanently reinvested, but rather the company will, over time, remit up foreign earnings and has provisioned for withholding taxes related to those earnings.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At December 31, 2020 and 2019, the Company had gross uncertain tax positions of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002077" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefits" contextRef="C_0001492633_20201231" decimals="-6" scale="6">149</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002076" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefits" contextRef="C_0001492633_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">164</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively. The Company has also accrued interest and penalties associated with these unrecognized tax benefits as of December 31, 2020 and 2019 of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002079" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsIncomeTaxPenaltiesAndInterestAccrued" contextRef="C_0001492633_20201231" decimals="-6" scale="6">26</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_002078" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsIncomeTaxPenaltiesAndInterestAccrued" contextRef="C_0001492633_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">25</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively. Estimated interest and penalties related to the underpayment of income taxes is classified as a component of benefit (provision) for income taxes in the Consolidated Statement of Operations. It is reasonably possible that within the next 12 months certain tax examinations will close, which could result in a change in unrecognized tax benefits, along with related interest and penalties. Furthermore, the amounts ultimately paid may differ from the amounts accrued. An estimate of any possible change cannot be made at this time.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.84%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Throughout 2019 and 2020, ongoing federal and international audits were effectively settled in certain tax jurisdictions and the impact was recorded in the financial statements.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.84%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">If the balance of the Company&#8217;s uncertain tax positions is sustained by the taxing authorities in the Company&#8217;s favor, the reversal of the entire balance would reduce the Company&#8217;s effective tax rate in future periods.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company files numerous consolidated and separate income tax returns in the U.S. Federal jurisdiction and in many state and foreign jurisdictions. With few exceptions, the Company is no longer subject to U.S. Federal income tax examinations for 2015 and prior periods. In addition, the Company has subsidiaries in various states, provinces and countries that are currently under audit for years ranging from 2007 through 2019. </p></ix:continuation>
